cf.title: BUG? Unpublished generated columns are reported "missing" by the subscription

input.subject: BUG? Unpublished generated columns are reported "missing" by the subscription

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic. Both raised objections (replication-ondisk-1, maintenance-fit-1) concerned committing 0002 without 0001, and the critic refuted them because 0002's own tests fail without 0001. The proposal fixes a confirmed v18 regression in tablesync, and two reviewers approved v2-0002. Open points are the back-patch plan and the review of 0001, which happens in another thread.

brief.title: Tablesync fails on tables with only unpublished generated columns
brief.problem: Since v18, initial table synchronization fails with "logical replication target relation ... is missing replicated column" when every column of a published table is an unpublished generated column. If the subscriber has a regular column of the same name, tablesync copies generated values that incremental replication never sends. It affects logical replication users with such tables, and only when copy_data is true.
brief.proposed_design: Tablesync also fetches whether pg_get_publication_tables() returned NULL attrs, and for v18+ publishers treats NULL as "no columns published" instead of "all columns". This leaves zero replicated columns, so the fix depends on a separate zero-column fix (0001) that adds BeginCopyFromExtended() so an explicitly empty COPY column list differs from an unspecified one.
user_visible_surface: C API: new BeginCopyFromExtended() in commands/copy.h, from the bundled 0001 patch; BeginCopyFrom() is unchanged.
Tablesync of tables with no published columns now succeeds and fills subscriber-only columns with their defaults.
author_claims: Older publishers are not affected because they exclude generated columns in the pg_attribute query.
Without 0001, text COPY loads '' instead of the local default and binary COPY fails with "row field count is 0".
The existing BeginCopyFrom() interface and behavior stay unchanged.
brief.thread_state: Shveta Malik confirmed the bug, Peter Smith reviewed v1 and approved v2-0002, and Shlok Kyal tested v2-0002 and approved it. No one reviewed 0001 in this thread; it belongs to a separate thread.
unclear: The material does not say whether the fix will be back-patched to v18, the release that introduced the bug.
Nothing says whether 0002 can be committed before 0001 or must wait for it.
The material does not say how a v18+ subscriber tells a NULL that means "no columns" from a NULL that means "no column list" when the publisher has an explicit column list.
Nothing says whether a new BeginCopyFromExtended() is acceptable in back branches.

refuted.title: Committing 0002 without 0001 turns a loud error into wrong subscriber data
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer pushes the reviewed 0002, or back-patches it to v18, before 0001 lands. A user subscribes to a table whose only column is VIRTUAL. Text-mode tablesync then stores '' in the subscriber-only column instead of its default, and nothing reports it until someone compares the rows.
refuted.argument: Message #3 says that without 0001 the text COPY loads '' and the binary COPY fails with "row field count is 0". Today the same case fails at once with "missing replicated column" (message #1). Peter Smith and Shlok Kyal approved only v2-0002 (messages #6, #7), and 0001 is reviewed in another thread. The proposal does not say that 0002 must wait for 0001, or that both go to the same branches together.
refuted.author_must_show: Will 0002 be committed and back-patched only together with 0001, and to which branches, given that 0002 alone gives silent wrong data in text mode?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 says the fix depends on the zero-column fix and bundles it as 0001 so that the tests pass. The 0002 tests cover text and binary mode, so 0002 pushed alone to any branch fails its own tests.

refuted.title: Fix needs a second COPY FROM entry point reviewed in another thread
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer back-patches 0002 to v18 without 0001, because only 0002 was reviewed here. Text-mode tablesync then stores '' in subscriber-only columns instead of their defaults, with no error. Users find out later, when they compare data on the subscriber.
refuted.argument: Message #3 says 0002 leaves zero replicated columns and is correct only on top of 0001. No one in this thread reviewed 0001 (messages #6 and #7 approve only v2-0002). 0001 adds BeginCopyFromExtended(), so COPY FROM gets a second entry point that has one caller today, and future changes to COPY setup must keep both paths in step. The material does not say whether 0001 goes to v18, the release that has the bug.
refuted.author_must_show: Will 0001 and 0002 be committed and back-patched together to v18, and could tablesync express an empty column list without adding a new exported COPY entry point?

critic.reasoning: The failure scenario duplicates replication-ondisk-1, and the 0002 tests guard against it. The entry-point concern names no concrete failure: the 0001 commit message says BeginCopyFrom() stays unchanged, and a new exported function does not break ABI in a back branch.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: 0002 changes how the tablesync worker reads NULL attrs from pg_get_publication_tables() for v18+ publishers.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: 0001 adds the exported function BeginCopyFromExtended() to commands/copy.h; BeginCopyFrom() stays unchanged.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The bug started in v18, but the CommitFest entry targets version 20 and the thread states no back-patch plan.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: COPY FROM gets a second entry point, BeginCopyFromExtended(), with tablesync as its only caller today.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will the fix be back-patched to v18, the release that introduced the bug, and will 0001 and 0002 go to the same branches together?
Is adding the exported BeginCopyFromExtended() acceptable in back branches, or does the back-branch fix need a different form?
When a v18+ publisher has an explicit column list, how does the subscriber tell NULL attrs meaning "no columns published" from NULL meaning "no column list"?
Must 0002 wait until 0001 is committed from its own thread, and who reviews 0001?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows logical replication tablesync and the COPY FROM setup code would have to own it; none has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the changed reading of NULL attrs in tablesync across publisher versions, and for a second COPY FROM entry point, in every branch that receives the fix.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a v2 after Peter Smith's review of v1, which shows follow-up during review; no sign either way for after commit.

priority.reason: The bug is a confirmed v18 regression that affects only tables whose columns are all unpublished generated columns. Both patches are small, touch tablesync and COPY FROM setup, and 0002 already has two approvals; 0001 still needs review in its own thread.

provisional_note: The code was not read, and only the first 3 of 7 messages were shown. Whether the NULL-attrs check handles explicit column lists and mixed publisher versions correctly, and whether 0001 resolves the empty list safely, could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: DOCS - Generated Column Logical Replication Examples
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an "Examples" subsection to the new "Generated Column Replication" documentation section. The examples are self-contained publication, subscription and table setups that show subtle rules, such as publication column lists overriding publish_generated_columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Only the opening message is shown, and the entry was later withdrawn without any visible reply or objection.

precedents_retrieved.title: DOCS for generated column replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Smith proposed an "Examples" subsection for the new "Generated Column Replication" documentation page. The patch adds a few self-contained publication and subscription examples, including one showing that a publication column list overrides publish_generated_columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila judged the current text and example sufficient, and preferred to wait for user feedback on the new feature before adding more examples. No one else supported the patch, so vignesh C closed the entry for lack of interest, open to revisit if users ask for it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This is a new feature, and I think it is better to
get some feedback from users. We can add more examples or information
based on real user feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: foreign key on virtual generated column
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows a foreign key on a virtual generated column, limited to ON UPDATE NO ACTION/RESTRICT and ON DELETE CASCADE/NO ACTION/RESTRICT. The RI check computes the generated value. ALTER COLUMN SET EXPRESSION and SET DATA TYPE then revalidate the constraint without a table rewrite.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only reviewer found the patches mostly fine and raised two performance points: the RI check computes virtual columns that are not in the key, and TryReuseForeignKey always forces revalidation when a virtual column is in the key. The visible messages contain no reply from the author before the withdrawal.

precedents_retrieved.title: generated columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Eisentraut proposed implementing SQL-standard generated columns (GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr)), with the generation expression stored in pg_attrdef like a default and MySQL/Oracle-style VIRTUAL|STORED syntax. Only the VIRTUAL (computed-on-read) variant was fully implemented; STORED, various ALTER TABLE forms and index support were deferred.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review by Jaime Casanova found multiple bugs: generated columns showed no value through a view, inheritance produced a malformed default and a server crash on insert, ALTER COLUMN TYPE on the referenced or generated column failed with internal errors, triggers saw NULL for the generated column, and the generation expression could be dropped via DROP DEFAULT. Based on these reviews, the commitfest manager marked the entry Returned with feedback, asking for an updated version to be resubmitted.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Based on this review, and the errors noted in upthread in the previous review,
I’m marking this Returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: COPY WHERE clause generated/system column reference
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patches make COPY FROM ... WHERE work with generated columns: they expand virtual generated columns in the WHERE clause and compute stored generated columns before the WHERE clause is checked. They also reject system columns other than tableoid in the WHERE clause.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed a smaller fix that rejects generated columns in COPY FROM WHERE with a clear error, and left tableoid for a separate thread. He then argued that support should not be added, because generated columns belong to the target table while the WHERE clause filters input data. Masahiko Sawada had shown that computing stored generated columns before the WHERE clause runs them before BEFORE INSERT triggers, so the WHERE clause changes the row the trigger sees.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This seems fundamentally wrong, because generated columns are a
property of the target table, but the COPY WHERE clause is meant to
filter the input data.

precedents_retrieved.title: Infinite Autovacuum loop caused by failing virtual generated column expression
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes ANALYZE skip an extended statistics object, with a WARNING, when evaluating one of its expressions raises an error, instead of failing for the whole table. The goal was to stop autovacuum from retrying a failing ANALYZE every cycle, as happens with extended statistics on an erroring virtual generated column.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed and Bharath Rupireddy saw the behaviour as expected: it has existed since expression statistics arrived in PG14, retries come about once a minute, a later retry may succeed, and the user can drop or fix the statistics object. Bharath also said a fix only for extended statistics is inconsistent with how autovacuum handles other ANALYZE errors. He found that v2 catches the error without re-throwing or aborting a subtransaction, which can leave an inconsistent state such as a non-empty SPI stack. He then withdrew the patch from the CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: After thinking about this more, I still prefer leaving the behaviour as-is (option 1).

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical decoding to output generated columns
precedents_retrieved.authors: Peter Smith (smithpb2250), Shubham Khanna (skhanna), Shlok Kyal (shlokkyal)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let pgoutput send generated column values in logical replication, so consumers get a complete row instead of computing generated columns on the subscriber. The work added replication of generated columns named in a publication column list, then a publish_generated_columns publication parameter.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Most of the work was committed before the entry closed: generated columns in column lists and the publish_generated_columns parameter. After that commit, Peter Eisentraut asked how the feature should work with the proposed virtual generated columns, which he thought could not be replicated, and Amit Kapila suggested limiting the option to stored generated columns. The thread then went idle in Waiting on Author, and Michael Paquier returned the entry until that question is settled.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As of now this thread is just waiting on author and idle in the CF app for no real purpose.

precedents_retrieved.title: Multi-column list partitioning
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds multi-column list partitioning, so that `partition by list (a, b)` takes partitions defined by value tuples such as `for values in (1, 2), (1, 5)`. It changes bound transformation, the bound data structures, tuple routing, partition pruning, NULL handling and, in a split second patch, partition-wise join.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amul Sul questioned the pruning design. Range partitioning needs a prefix of the partition keys, but list partitions could also be pruned on later keys alone, and he judged the NULL handling in pruning to be wrong. Julien Rouhaud set the entry to Waiting on Author because of these concerns and a clang warning. The visible messages show no new patch or author reply before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I haven't studied the whole partition pruning code and don't know the complete code flow, but AFAICU, this is not the correct way to handle null value.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P7] added publish_generated_columns and closed idle over how virtual generated columns should replicate, which does not apply to this tablesync bugfix. The thread links only to the zero-column COPY discussion, as the source of 0001 (messages #1, #3, #5), and reports no earlier rejection of this fix.

No standards or compatibility objection holds. The fix adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or psql change, and makes tablesync match incremental replication. The C API is additive, since BeginCopyFrom() keeps its behaviour. Back-patch status and the dependency on 0001 are open, but no failure scenario follows from them for existing users.

The proposal does not change the on-disk format, WAL, the catalogs or the wire protocol. The new BeginCopyFromExtended() only adds a function. The v18+ publisher version check covers subscribers that connect to older publishers.

The proposal has no new privilege or exposure aspect. It adds no new role, GUC, SQL entry point or default. Subscriber-only columns get their defaults through the usual COPY path, which already runs the subscriber's default expressions and triggers. The fix also stops tablesync from copying generated values that the publication does not publish, which narrows exposure. BeginCopyFromExtended() is an internal C API and not reachable from SQL.

This is a narrow, confirmed bug fix in tablesync. It has no hot-path cost and adds nothing users must configure, and two logical replication reviewers approved 0002. The only maintenance concern is its dependency on 0001.

This is a bug fix in tablesync for a v18 regression. No existing feature, option or extension gives correct initial sync for tables whose only columns are unpublished generated columns. copy_data = false avoids the error but skips the initial copy, so it does not do the same job. BeginCopyFromExtended() follows the usual practice of adding a variant entry point and keeping the old one stable, and it does not duplicate a separate mechanism.

This is a confirmed v18 regression in tablesync that can copy generated values incremental replication never sends, so demand evidence is not the test. The affected tables are rare, but a correctness fix carries no user-facing cost, and [P7] concerns the feature itself, not this bug.
